subject: general
question: Which of the following bills presented along with the Annual Financial Statement provides details on the imposition, abolition, remission, alteration or regulation of taxes proposed in the Budget in India?
solution:
The correct answer is the __**Finance Bill**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Finance Bill is **presented along with the Annual Financial Statement and provides details on the imposition, abolition, remission, alteration or regulation of taxes proposed in the Budget in India
 
• The term *budget* is nowhere been used in the constitution it is the popular name for the annual financial statement which comes in Article 112.
 
• Financial bills are those bills that deal with fiscal matters that is revenue or expenditure.
 
• The Finance Bill **helps the Government to implement its decisions related to imposition, abolition, or remission of taxes.**
 
• Any matters related to the regulation of money borrowed by the Government of India or the money which is there in the Consolidated Fund of India is also covered by the Finance Bill.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Money Bill**

 
 
• **​**These **bills are concerned with financial matters like taxation, public expenditure, borrowing, audits, and accounting**.
 
• The Speaker of the Lok Sabha has the final authority to determine if a bill is a money bill.
 
• **Money bills can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha with the prior recommendation of the President**
 
 
 
• **Ordinary Bill**
 
 
• **​**These bills **are concerned with any matter other than financial subjects.**
 
• Any ordinary law needs to be passed by both Houses
 
 
 
• **Ordinance Replacing Bill**
 
 
• **​**These **bills are brought before Parliament to replace an ordinance with or without modifications promulgated by the President. **
 
 
 
• **Once a bill is passed in one house, it is sent to the other house for consideration. **
 
• **The second house goes through a similar procedure of readings, debates, and voting. **
 
• **If the second house suggests any amendments, the bill is sent back to the first house. **
